page: The Vultr vhf-1c-1gb is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It is provisioned with 1 shared x86_64 vCPU powered by an Intel processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, 1.0 GB of RAM, and 32 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions are absent. The instance lacks dedicated GPU hardware and includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reflects performance constraints typical of a single shared core and 1.0 GB memory footprint. Single-thread workloads register moderate output, with stress-ng single-core achieving 1865.79 and gzip single-threaded compression reaching 28.26 GB/sec, placing both in the average tier. Bzip3 decompression yielded 9.41 GB/sec. Across broader tests, overall throughput ranks in lower percentiles. The PassMark CPU score is 2239.98, PassMark memory registers at 974.54, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 16.75 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput achieved 1.94 GB/sec, while Redis recorded 2.19 million SET operations per second.

The shared single-vCPU architecture and 1.0 GB memory ceiling limit this instance from handling parallel execution, high-concurrency database transactions, or memory-intensive runtimes. However, bundled high-speed NVMe storage provides low-latency local I/O relative to standard shared hosting. The vhf-1c-1gb offers high cost efficiency for entry-tier compute workloads such as lightweight microservices, jump boxes, small automation tasks, test environments, and low-traffic static web servers.
